Leo: Heads up — ~18% p99 latency regression on qwen2.5 after the prefetcher change. Seen on mixed CJK+latin prompts. KernelChooser is picking 'matmul-fallback' for a bunch of steps instead of the usual fused_gemm. Anyone else? :thinking:
Anita: Which commit / instance?
Leo: aws-g5dn, commit 9f3d2b2 -> pushed the prefetch batching tweak earlier today. Quick trace attached below.
Leo: ```
# flamegraph snippet
fused_gemm  (expected)  0.72s
matmul-fallback         1.33s  <-- spike
KVCache::misses          12% -> 46%
seq_len distribution: median=92, 95p=410, outliers to 1200 (CJK tokenization)
```
Sara: interesting — CJK prompts tend to explode token counts. Prefetcher may be shifting batch boundaries so the kernel heuristic sees different seq_len distribution.
Max: Also noticed kernel chooser weights were tuned against english-only histograms. If token counts jump, the heuristic might flip to a safer kernel.
PerfBot: Automated profile: regression detected on qwen2.5-serving /slot-3 — +17.9% p99, +7.4% median. Top blame: kernel_selection (35%), kv_cache_eviction (28%), batching_fragments (14%). Link: https://perf/reports/2523456789
Anita: Can we repro locally with the same tokenize pipeline? If the tokenizer is returning many subtokens for CJK, combined batching+prefetch reorder can increase cross-request mem pressure and evict KV pages.
Rachel: I'll make a tiny reproducer. Suggest we try: (1) tokenizing a mixed CJK/EN set, (2) run with prefetcher on/off, (3) dump kernel_choice log + kv hit/miss.
Leo: repro script attached — runs 500 requests with mix of 1-3 short english + 1 CJK long prompt. With prefetcher=on we see 3x more kv invalidations.
Max: Hypothesis: prefetcher consolidates micro-batches which changes the time-locality of KV accesses; combined with our eviction threshold (max_cached_kv_bytes) it forces earlier evictions. When the kernel selector inspects samples it sees increased effective seq_len and picks matmul-fallback to avoid memory blowups.
Anita: Two options: revert prefetch merge, or change kernel selection logic to be less sensitive to single-batch outliers. Which is lower risk?
Leo: Quick patch tested: increase kernel_selector::robustness_penalty for fallback by +0.15 so it prefers fused_gemm unless fallback is clearly better. Small canary shows p99 back to baseline but kv miss rate still slightly up.
Sara: That sounds like masking the real issue. We should address KV eviction + batching alignment. Maybe prefetcher should annotate original request boundaries so eviction heuristic uses per-request rather than consolidated batch footprint.
Max: Agree. Longer fix: have prefetcher emit an optional metadata field 'logical_batch_map' so KVCache can compute retention per-original-request. Short fix: tune max_cached_kv_bytes up on slot-3 to avoid evictions during consolidation.
DeployBot: Canary rollout queued: rollback-prefetcher -> 5% -> 50% -> full if no regressions.
Rachel: I pushed reproducer + logs to the ticket: INF-5924. Added perf traces and kernel_choice dumps.
PerfBot: Regression ticket INF-5924 created. Assignees: @Leo @Sara @Anita.
Anita: Next actions:
- Rachel/Leo: run reproducer with prefetcher off/on, attach raw token counts (by position)
- Max: experiment with kernel_selector penalty and report microbench
- Sara: prototype logical_batch_map for KV retention (small PR)
Plan: revert prefetcher in slot-3 for now (DeployBot), iterate on logical retention + smarter kernel heuristic.
Leo: Thanks — will start the local runs now. Will post numbers in this thread. :eyes:
